item.title: Mass. ‘Micromobility’ Commission Recommends Improved Classification, Regulation of Motorbikes and Scooters
item.description: Among other recommendations, the commission supports expanding bikeshare systems and other micromobility options as a safer, less expensive, and more efficient alternative to driving.

item.title: Sunbelt Cities Rank Last in National Street Safety Index
item.description: Cars and drivers continue to dominate the newest and sunniest cities in the United States.

item.title: Why Anti-Trans Laws Are Terrible For Transportation, Too
item.description: A disturbing new Kansas law revokes trans people's driver's licenses. Here's how it will make our communities more dangerous.

item.title: Monday’s Headlines Took the Keys Away
item.description: A demographic disaster is coming as a generation of aging suburbanites become either dangerous drivers or trapped in their homes.

item.title: Exactly How Much It Cost to Build the Average Parking Space In Your City
item.description: For new apartments, the research found that building required parking adds roughly $50,000 to $100,000 per unit, and disproportionately increases the cost to build smaller apartments.

item.title: How the ‘Little Free Pantry’ Can Help Feed the Hungry Without Requiring Them to Drive
item.description: Researchers are trying to reduce the mobility barrier to food by bringing it directly to neighborhoods.

item.title: Could Refurbished E-Bikes Be the Secret Weapon of the Livable Streets Movement?
item.description: A high-quality used market could be the boost America needs to get would-be riders off the sidelines and into the saddle, a new report argues.

item.title: Tuesday’s Headlines Are a Little Bit Safer
item.description: Traffic deaths are down about 12 percent, which the National Safety Council attributes to new technology and infrastructure investments.

item.title: Dear Trump: the Future Belongs to the Efficient
item.description: Trump abandoned climate protection goals claiming that cheap fossil fuel helps consumers and the economy. A mobility-focused analysis shows that he is wrong: resource efficiency is the key to health, economic success and happiness.

item.title: Wednesday’s Headlines Don’t Got a Fast Car
item.description: If Tracy Chapman had saved "just a little bit of money" these days, she'd be in trouble.
